question.text: Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo></math> be squares such that for each <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi><mo>⩾</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo></math> the length of the side of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></math> equals the length of diagonal of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math>. If the length of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>12</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>, then the smallest value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math> for which area of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></math> is less than one, is

solution.text:
Let an be the side length of An.

So, an=2an+1,a1=12

⇒ an=12×12n-1

Now, an2<1⇒1442n-1<1

⇒ 2n-1>144

⇒ n-1≥8

⇒ n≥9
